blocks.text: After you configure a user portal, Private Access (ZPA) generates a canonical name (CNAME) that must be published in your public DNS. When a user's web browser resolves to the user portal URL, they need to be authenticated against their identity provider (IdP). After authentication, the user portal is displayed along with all associated application links. The user can only view links to applications they are allowed to access. To learn more, see About User Portal Links.

For an end user to access a user portal, at least one SAML attribute needs to be configured for your IdP in Private Access. To learn more, see About SAML Attributes and Configuring an IdP for Single Sign-On.

The authentication timeout for a user portal session is based on the default timeout policy rule. If you edit the rule, the change does not immediately impact any currently authenticated user portal sessions. When an end user's session expires, the user portal might become unresponsive. If this occurs, they need to reauthenticate into the portal to continue accessing applications.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Browser > Clientless Portal > User Portals.
Click Add.

blocks.text: The Add User Portal drawer opens.

blocks.item: In the Add User Portal drawer:
Name: Enter a name for the portal. The name cannot contain special characters, with the exception of periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).
Status: Make sure Enabled is selected. If disabled, the portal is inaccessible to users.
Certificate Type: Select either Managed or Custom.
If you select Managed, the portal certificate is managed by Zscaler.
Complete the following steps.
In the Portal URL field, enter the domain prefix.
Select the domain suffix from the drop-down menu.
Click the Copy icon to copy the URL.
See image.
If you select Custom, you can select an existing certificate.
Complete the following steps.
In the URL field, enter the full URL for the portal that users will access. The URL must use the HTTPS protocol and be a fully qualified domain name (FQDN).
A user portal's FQDN cannot be configured as an application within an application segment.

From the Portal Server Certificate drop-down menu, select the certificate that is associated with the portal. Click the Delete icon next to the certificate to deselect it. To learn more, see About (Web Server) Certificates.
The certificate must support the FQDN specified for the portal.
See image.
Description: (Optional) Enter a description for the portal.
Notification Banner: If you want to display a notification to your users at the top of the portal page:
Status: Select Enabled to display a banner.
Message Text: Enter the notification text that you want displayed in the portal's banner.
See image.
Click Save.

blocks.text: For user portals with a custom certificate, complete the following steps:

blocks.item: On the User Portals page, expand the name of the user portal to view its details, then click the Copy icon next to the Canonical Name (CNAME). You need this CNAME record for your public DNS.
Add the CNAME information you copied to your public DNS, and verify that the FQDN for the user portal resolves to the record.

blocks.text: Zscaler automatically manages the public DNS for the FQDN of user portals with a Zscaler-managed certificate.
